lirael.title: Whoever Finds This
lirael.text: Lirael meets Sam at the old iron postbox in the alley after close, a single lamp throwing their shadows long across the cobbles. From her satchel she draws a yellowed letter, soft at the folds from years of handling: the very first one, addressed to "Whoever finds this." She reads it aloud in a clear, careful clerk's voice that trembles at the end. "I never thought anyone would write back." Her long ears are drooping, and her fingers smooth the paper as if it might tear. "And then you did."

choices.label: "Thank you for writing first."
choices.res: Her satchel strap slips from her fingers and clinks against the cobbles, loud in the quiet alley. She covers her face with the letter, ears trembling, and does not seem to mind that he can see.

choices.label: Take the letter and read your own reply
choices.res: He reads it aloud from memory, and she mouths the words along with him; she has known them by heart for years. When he stumbles over a line she supplies it, softly, without looking.

image.comp: holding a yellowed letter against her chest beside an old iron postbox, long ears drooping, shy and tearful smile
image.setting: lamp-lit alley beside an old iron postbox at night

lirael.title: Ink Stains
lirael.text: Sam opens the washroom door and finds Lirael in the tub, a stack of waterproofed letters balanced on the rim, reading with a soft smile and a damp pencil behind one long ear. She looks up. Her hand slaps the water and a fan of drops lands across the top page. "I read them here," she says, mortified, pressing the letters to her chest. "It's the only quiet room in the building."

choices.label: Apologize and back out
choices.res: "It's fine!" she squeaks. That evening a note appears under his door, three neat lines in her sorter's hand, signed with a tiny drawn quill that has blotted a little at the tip.

choices.label: "Which one are you on?"
choices.res: She holds up the letter. He reads it from the doorway, politely addressing the ceiling. She laughs so hard the water sloshes, and the ink on the rim runs in a pretty blue stream.

choices.label: Stand there, flustered
choices.res: The tips of her ears go pink. "Please say something," she whispers. He tries, fails, and she giggles into her hands, a rare, bubbling sound that echoes off the wooden walls.

image.comp: reading a letter in a tub with a stack of letters on the rim, long ears perked up in surprise, hand splashing the water

lirael.title: Notes Across the Sofa
lirael.text: They fall into an easy habit: sitting at opposite ends of the lounge sofa after close, writing each other notes instead of talking, and passing them across with their feet. It is a ridiculous, wonderful way to flirt. The fire ticks, paper rustles, and Lirael's replies grow longer every night, her handwriting looping as she gets braver. Tonight's note has a P.S. in very small letters, crowded into the corner like a secret.

choices.label: Stay with her
choices.res: He reads the P.S. aloud, and she buries her face in a cushion, ears trembling, then scribbles a reply and kicks it across the sofa before she can think better of it.

choices.label: Write one back about how you feel
choices.res: She reads it three times, mouthing the words, then folds it into precise thirds and tucks it into her satchel, beside the others, where he can see how many there are.

image.comp: curled at one end of a sofa writing a note on her knee, one foot swinging, peeking over the paper with a shy smile

lirael.title: Wrong Address
lirael.text: A letter arrives for Sam with no stamp, no postmark, and an address in a handwriting he hasn't used in years: his own, from long ago. It reads: "To whoever I become. I hope you're not lonely anymore." Lirael reads over his shoulder, and the sorting-room hum around them seems to fade. She goes very still, long ears flat. "If a letter can cross," she says quietly, "so can a person. What if the box takes you back?"

choices.label: "I'm not going anywhere."
choices.res: She nods, and holds his sleeve for a long time anyway, thumb worrying the cuff, as though it were a letter she might lose in the post.

choices.label: Write a reply together
choices.res: They write two words and post them: Not lonely. The old box hums under her palm, a low warm note. She is still smiling when it falls silent.

choices.label: Burn the letter
choices.res: "You can't burn what's already happened," she says. She spends the night sweeping the postbox in silence, one slow stroke after another, ears low.

image.comp: reading a letter over his shoulder, ears drooped, fear in her eyes

lirael.title: Full Moon Post
lirael.text: Under a full moon Lirael takes Sam up onto the post house roof to sort the night's collection by lantern light, bundles tied with twine, the slate cold beneath them. She lets her shoulders and ears relax, her clerk's stiffness softening in the silver air. Between letters, she hums the tune she once wrote in the margin of her second note, and he realizes he's been humming it for years without knowing where it came from.

choices.label: Hum along
choices.res: She stops sorting and just listens, ears tilted toward him, and then joins the harmony in a thin sweet voice. The letters lie forgotten in her lap.

choices.label: Help her sort the last bag
choices.res: He puts every letter in the wrong slot. She re-sorts every one, grinning, and says it's the best mistake she's ever seen, and keeps the worst-sorted one to herself.

image.comp: sitting on a post house roof in moonlight sorting letters, long ears relaxed, humming, glancing at him with soft eyes
image.setting: slate rooftop under a full moon, a lantern beside her

lirael.title: Meeting the Man
lirael.text: Lirael sets her satchel down in the doorway of Sam's room, a thing she has never done in front of him. "For ten years I wrote to a name," she says. "I'd like to meet the man." She is trembling, ears dipping, one foot hooked around her own ankle. "I'm not good at saying things out loud. So I'll say the short version." She takes his hand, and her ink-stained fingertips are warm. "Stay." The door closes behind them.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.res: Lirael nods and straightens her satchel strap, gracious as a clerk with a delayed parcel. "I can wait," she says. "I've waited longer for less. Just do write back."
